reviewContext.issueReference: workflowInput:session-718 right-drag-pan contextmenu regression (no GitHub issue; follow-up to commit 30f411a)
reviewContext.userProblem: In the real macOS debug app, a right-drag on a preview (observed on a PDF) does not pan. WebKit fires contextmenu at right mouse down, before any pointermove. The contextMenu handler in attachPreviewPan (src/features/preview/previewPanZoom.ts:282-286) only prevents the menu after a moved right gesture, so the native Reload / Inspect Element menu opens and takes the drag.
requiredOutcomes: contextmenu on a preview pan target is prevented at event time (including press time) unless window.getSelection().toString() is non-empty or the target (or a text node's parent) is inside input, textarea or [contenteditable] other than "false". An active or just-ended right pan always prevents it.
Regression vitest: contextmenu at right pointerdown before any move is prevented, and later pointermoves beyond the slop still pan the container.

Old assertions that a plain right-click or a post-middle contextmenu is not prevented are replaced in previewPanZoom.vitest.ts, PreviewPane.vitest.tsx, MediaFilePreviewPane.vitest.tsx and PdfFilePreviewPane.vitest.tsx.
README.md:254 no longer promises the native menu on a plain right-click.
Pan, slop, chord release, fling and wheel zoom are unchanged.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Put the guard inside the existing contextMenu handler of attachPreviewPan, with a module-private keepsNativeContextMenu(event: MouseEvent): boolean predicate.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: The listener already exists only on the preview pan targets. This is the smallest diff (architecture.md#pan-gesture-contract).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: Keep the suppressMenu post-drag flag, and give it priority over the selection and editable exemptions.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Keeps the post-pan behavior on Windows, where contextmenu follows release. The chord-release assertion stays valid.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: The selection check is any non-empty window selection without trim. The editable check is closest('input, textarea, [contenteditable]:not([contenteditable="false"])') on event.target or a text node's parentElement.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Follows the nodetto keepsNativeContextMenu behavior. The no-trim divergence was accepted in design review.

intentionalTradeoffs: A plain right-click over previews no longer shows Reload or Inspect Element on any platform.
With a non-empty selection, a right press on macOS still opens the native menu and does not pan.
Real WebKit press-time ordering is verified only by the supervising GUI re-check.
supportedEdgeCases: contextmenu dispatched at right pointerdown before any pointermove (macOS WebKit order) is prevented, and later moves past the slop still pan the container.
contextmenu after release (Windows order) following a right pan is prevented by the just-ended flag, which any contextmenu consumes and the next pointerdown clears.
A plain right-click with no gesture, and contextmenu after middle or left gestures, are prevented.
Targets inside input, textarea or [contenteditable] (including contenteditable="") keep the native menu; contenteditable="false" with no editable ancestor is prevented.
Text-node event targets resolve through parentElement for the editable check.
Any non-empty window selection (no trim) keeps the native menu, except while a right pan is active or has just ended.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Context menus outside the preview pan targets (no global, window or document guard).
Editables inside shadow DOM (composedPath is not used).
Whitespace-only selections (the selection is not trimmed).
Canvas, video and link specific exemptions.
Real macOS WebKit press-time ordering in automated tests (covered only by the supervising GUI re-check).

acceptanceCriteria: contextmenu with no gesture, no selection and a non-editable target is defaultPrevented.
contextmenu right after a right pointerdown, before any move, is prevented, and later moves past the slop pan the container (scrollLeft 90).
Editable targets and a non-empty selection keep the native menu unless a right pan is active or has just ended.
Existing pan, chord, fling, wheel and geometry tests pass. Only the three listed menu assertions change.
